meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone talk to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen first.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing those down. Owen drafts somewhere else and pastes it in when it's finished, so all that shows me is a paste.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays between us, not in front of his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, Hale. A wrong line is a mistake, not proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then say what you're proposing, and say it precisely.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Arguments change between an outline and a final draft. I asked what you're proposing, Hale.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing tonight, and I'll read every line of it. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want the date and time of it in that email, and it's before December 1.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll ask him tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in your email, and the room.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still want that in writing with Thursday the twelfth and the room in it, and an answer to my question of whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. You said I would have this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record; she still wants it in writing tonight with the date and room, and an answer on whether Owen was heard first. This is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you got there with time to spare.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her paste defence by inviting Owen to bring a dated draft, which gave her something specific she could check and no room to wave it away.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you ground, though you never answered her opening question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, and she carried that into her email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of night. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after owning the zero, answer her first question directly by saying whether you spoke to Owen before entering it, as procedure 4.1 requires, so it can't become an open point in her email.
